title: Is It My Fault That I Got Bullied?

chapters.title: The Reunion
content: Aizawa attends his middle school reunion after twenty years
He sees Suzuki, the boy who mercilessly bullied him and caused him to drop out of school.
Suzuki is now a successful banker and seems to have no regrets about his past actions .
Suzuki coldly dismisses Aizawa's presence and makes a cruel statement: 'There's a reason why some people get bullied' .
Aizawa is furious but remains silent, revealing nothing.
He has a secret that Suzuki does not know: Aizawa is now a middle school teacher
Suzuki's beloved daughter, Shiori, is one of his students.
Aizawa reflects on the years of torment he endured because of Suzuki.
The reunion ends with Aizawa watching Suzuki leave, a plan forming in his mind.
Aizawa wonders if Suzuki will ever face consequences for his actions.

chapters.title: The Teacher's Secret
content: Aizawa begins his new role at the middle school where Shiori is a student
He presents himself as a competent and caring teacher
Shiori appears to be a normal, happy student with no idea about her father's past.
Aizawa observes the social dynamics of the school carefully.
He notices that Shiori is being targeted by a group of bullies .
Aizawa is initially conflicted about what to do.
The bullying of Shiori escalates, and the school administration does nothing .
Aizawa sees a reflection of his own past suffering in Shiori's situation.
He decides to use his position to protect Shiori while also planning his revenge against Suzuki .
Aizawa believes that the sins of the father must be paid for by the family.

chapters.title: The Bullying Begins
content: Shiori is subjected to a harassment campaign at school
The bullies spread rumors, steal her belongings, and humiliate her in class.
Shiori feels increasingly isolated and scared.
Her parents, especially her father Shinji Suzuki, are unaware of the severity of the situation.
Suzuki, focused on his banking career, dismisses Shiori's initial complaints.
The school's head teacher tries to cover up the bullying to save the school's reputation .
Aizawa documents all the incidents of bullying against Shiori.
He intervenes when he can, but the bullies remain undeterred.
Shiori begins to question herself, echoing her father's cruel words: 'Is it my fault?' .
Aizawa knows that he needs to gather more evidence to take decisive action.

chapters.title: A Father's Complacency
content: Suzuki is confronted with evidence of his daughter's suffering.
He is shocked but remains arrogant and refuses to take full responsibility.
Suzuki tries to use his money and influence to solve the problem quietly.
He pressures the school to discipline the bullies without causing a scandal.
The school administration caves to Suzuki's demands.
Aizawa is disgusted by Suzuki's behavior and the school's complicity.
He uses his knowledge of Suzuki's past to manipulate him.
Aizawa reminds Suzuki of his own words: 'There's a reason why some people get bullied'
Suzuki begins to feel the first pangs of unease and fear.
He realizes that Aizawa is not just a teacher; he is an avenger.

chapters.title: The First Strike
content: Aizawa begins to implement his revenge plan.
He anonymously leaks information about Suzuki's past to the media.
The story about the successful banker who was a childhood bully starts to circulate online.
Suzuki's colleagues and clients begin to question his character.
Suzuki's perfect life starts to crack.
He becomes paranoid and lashes out at everyone around him.
Aizawa watches Suzuki's downfall with grim satisfaction.
However, he also feels a sense of emptiness and guilt.
Aizawa realizes that revenge is more complicated than he imagined.
He begins to question his own motivations and methods.

chapters.title: The Bullies' Motivation
content: The manga explores the backstories of the girls bullying Shiori
One bully comes from an abusive home environment.
Another feels immense pressure from her family to perform academically.
The leader of the bullies is insecure and fears being left out of her social group.
Their tragic pasts are used to explain their toxic behavior.
However, the manga is criticized for making the villains too one-dimensional .
Shiori remains a victim, and her character development is limited.
Aizawa struggles to feel empathy for the bullies despite their troubled pasts.
He remembers that he also had a difficult childhood but never became a bully.
Aizawa's anger towards the bullies and Suzuki remains intense.

chapters.title: The School's Failure
content: The story emphasizes the systemic failure of the school to address bullying .
Teachers are portrayed as either incompetent or complicit.
The head teacher prioritizes the school's reputation over students' well-being.
Aizawa is one of the few teachers who actually cares about the victims.
He clashes with the school administration over their negligence.
Aizawa tries to implement better anti-bullying policies.
The administration blocks his attempts, fearing negative publicity.
The manga criticizes how bullying is often covered up in Japan
Aizawa becomes more determined to expose the school's failures.
He knows that the system will never change unless it is forced to.

chapters.title: The Escalation
content: The bullying against Shiori becomes more brutal.
She is physically harmed and her mental health deteriorates.
Shiori's grades drop, and she withdraws from all social activities.
Suzuki finally sees the full extent of his daughter's suffering.
He breaks down and apologizes to Shiori for not believing her sooner.
Suzuki attempts to confront Aizawa, accusing him of manipulating the situation.
Aizawa reveals that he has been gathering evidence for months.
He threatens to expose Suzuki and the school to the authorities.
Suzuki is terrified and begs Aizawa for mercy.
Aizawa delivers a powerful speech about the lasting damage of bullying.

chapters.title: The Reckoning
content: Aizawa finally achieves his long-awaited revenge .
He exposes Suzuki's past and the school's cover-up to the police and the media.
Suzuki is arrested and faces public disgrace.
The bullies who tormented Shiori are expelled and face criminal charges.
The school administration is also punished for its negligence.
Aizawa's revenge is complete, but it is a hollow victory.
He realizes that his quest for revenge has consumed his life
Aizawa's actions are controversial, and some see him as a monster .
He has become the very thing he sought to destroy.
Aizawa reflects on the cost of his revenge.

chapters.title: The Aftermath
content: The fallout from Aizawa's actions affects everyone involved.
Suzuki's family is destroyed by his disgrace.
Shiori is left traumatized and scarred by her experiences.
The bullies are forced to confront the consequences of their cruelty.
Aizawa is hailed as a hero by some and vilified as a villain by others.
He struggles to find a reason to continue living.
The story shows that revenge does not heal the wounds of the past.
Aizawa finally understands the title's question: 'Is it my fault that I got bullied?'
He knows that the answer is a resounding 'no.'
But he also knows that the answer to 'Is it my fault for getting revenge?' is more complex.

chapters.title: The Final Lesson
content: The manga concludes with Aizawa visiting Shiori in the hospital.
He apologizes to her for his part in her suffering.
Shiori forgives Aizawa, showing incredible strength and resilience.
Aizawa realizes that true justice is not about revenge.
It is about creating a world where bullying is no longer tolerated.
He decides to dedicate his life to helping victims of bullying.
The manga ends with Aizawa opening a support center for bullied children.
The story delivers a powerful message: it is never the victim's fault .
The series emphasizes the need for empathy, accountability, and systemic change.
It challenges readers to confront the problem of bullying in their own communities.
